teaser: Eight kinds of reader, none of them attackers, nine ways to cheat a browser meter, and the quieter risks that will actually happen.
core_idea: A reading meter kept entirely in the browser can be cheated by anyone, but the people who could cheat are readers, not attackers; sized on a ladder from invisible engineers (about 0.6% of internet users are developers) to people who cannot use a computer (26% of OECD adults), with agents moving between steps, the cheating costs the site nothing it would have had, while the risks that will actually happen are confusion, a shared computer exposing history and card fraud, so the design is aimed at the readers who will pay and at not frightening the rest.

nodes.label: Who are you protecting against, one level down
nodes.summary: Kinds of reader instead of tiers of attacker; none malicious.

nodes.label: Eight kinds of reader
nodes.summary: Invisible, agents, power users, instruction followers, pragmatic payers, little understanding, mixed, struggling.

nodes.label: Agents change level in a single request
nodes.summary: Outside the meter by design; reading the markdown twin is not metered.

nodes.label: Nine ways to cheat or leak
nodes.summary: Devtools, private window, forged return page, replay, clearing data, agents, shared computer, injected script, card fraud.

nodes.label: Cheating costs nothing that reaches the site
nodes.summary: It changes a number only the cheater sees and removes a payment that was never coming.

nodes.label: The risks that will actually happen
nodes.summary: Confusion at the bottom of the ladder, shared-computer history, card fraud on the payment link.

nodes.label: Aim at the readers who will pay
nodes.summary: Do not build for step 1 at the expense of steps 5 to 8.

nodes.label: 26% of adults cannot use a computer
nodes.summary: OECD Survey of Adult Skills via Nielsen Norman Group: only 5% at the most skilled level.

nodes.label: Developers are about 0.6% of internet users
nodes.summary: 36.5 million professional developers against about 6.0 billion internet users.

quotes.text: An agent is not a step; it is a lift.
quotes.why: Agents move between levels of sophistication in a single request.

quotes.text: The struggling reader is protected by the meter asking nothing of them.
quotes.why: Why the usability work is aimed at the bottom of the ladder.

quotes.text: No button leads to the free one.
quotes.why: The unprotected return page is documented, but the payment is the default route.
